This issue is not VRChat's responsibility to fix. This is a common issue with Unity when dealing with direct texture creation (which AVPro/UnityVP do in the background).

The issue stems from how platform differences affect the texture drawing direction. (https://docs.unity3d.com/2022.3/Documentation/Manual/SL-PlatformDifferences.html)

Specifically:

> Vertical Texture coordinate conventions differ between two types of platforms: Direct3D-like and OpenGL-like.

> 

> Direct3D-like: The coordinate is 0 at the top and increases downward. This applies to Direct3D, Metal and consoles.

> OpenGL-like: The coordinate is 0 at the bottom and increases upward. This applies to OpenGL and OpenGL ES.

>

> This difference tends not to have any effect on your project, other than when rendering into a Render Texture.

> When rendering into a Texture on a Direct3D-like platform, Unity internally flips rendering upside down. This makes the conventions match between platforms, with the OpenGL-like platform convention the standard.

UnityVP handles this fine, AVPro (clearly) does not. This is something that AVPro itself must address.

This is the reason all (sane) existing video players explicitly pass in/have a parameter in their rendering process/shader when AVPro is present so the texture can be correctly flipped when needed. Any change to this expectation of incorrect texture flipping WILL cause the video to become flipped undesirably in existing worlds.

original text for posterity:

Hi,

in VRC we have 2 alternative underlying players, Unity (sometimes called "Video") and AVPro (sometimes called "Stream").

for some reason the AVPro player had reversed V coordinate of the UV, so people ended up adding hacks to their video player shaders like

```

    #if UNITY_UV_STARTS_AT_TOP

    if (_IsAVProInput)

    {

        uv = float2(uv.x, 1 - uv.y);

    }

    #endif

```

src: https://github.com/MerlinVR/USharpVideo/blob/master/Assets/USharpVideo/Shaders/StandardVideoCore.cginc#L58

however, some time ago AVPro player (at least in USharpVideo player prefab) started showing the video upside-down on Quest standalone.

removing the code mentioned above from the shader makes it work just fine... but it breaks (reverses) on PC,

so the conclusion is that the Quest's AVPro player now has correct UVs but at the same time kept the now-incorrect declaration of UNITY_UV_STARTS_AT_TOP

the worst part in all this is that it seems to be not easily workaroundable, because i can't find anything that would help me distinguish a PC vs Quest build in the shader.

please either

a) update(?) the AVPro on PC so it doesn't require the UV reversal either,

b) alternatively, stop declaring the UNITY_UV_STARTS_AT_TOP for Quest's AVPro,

c) alternatively, declare a define/shader keyword that will distinguish the build between PC/Quest and allow us to work around it,

d) or if all else fails, revert the change on Quest so we can just revert them both and get the valid result.

technically, i checked it between live quest version and beta PC, but it's been an issue for a while and i don't think it affects anything here
title: Inconsistently reversed V of the UV in AVPro players
